correctness.rationale: For nonzero dyadic valuation v>=2, the exact map v->v+nu_2(v)-1 is proved; even-block cases reduce k=nu_2(v) via the strictly decreasing map T(k), with terminal k=1 fixed or k=2 primitive two-cycle. The shift m+1 yields exact terminal labels. The residue-class decomposition gives alpha=sum_{r:F(r)=2}2^{-r} with O(log N) discrepancy. Explicit unbounded fibers of F=1 and F=2 and the shift-by-any-period contradiction show its binary digit sequence cannot be eventually periodic, hence alpha is irrational. Two direct finite algorithms verified 99999 initial exponents but do not replace any infinite proof.

value.rationale: The published literature identifies an arithmetic partial derivative with bounded valuation period, making the distribution of its two terminal orbit types a natural exact invariant. The result evaluates this distribution up to logarithmic discrepancy and proves its limiting density irrational by a structural recursive argument. No broader theorem or application is asserted; the explicit distinction between sample spaces avoids a spurious significance claim.
